key_insight: The paper shows that relativistic detonation waves can be accurately captured with an ALE finite-volume solver and that, unlike the Newtonian case, the Zel'dovich pressure jump is nonmonotonic with mass flux.
engineering_relevance: This matters for high-speed reactive-flow modeling in astrophysics and relativistic propulsion/energy-extraction studies, where shock tracking and stiff chemistry must be handled robustly.
method: Second-order finite-volume ALE scheme with TVD reconstruction.
Mesh velocity chosen to match the shock speed for sharp front tracking.
Locally implicit treatment of stiff reaction source terms plus an efficient conserved-to-primitive variable conversion algorithm.
evidence_signal: The solver successfully reproduces the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering detonation profile up to shock Lorentz factors of about 7.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness depend on a nontrivial conserved-to-primitive conversion and careful handling of stiff reaction terms, which may complicate implementation.
paper_title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
